title: 1960 AHSME Problem 27
statement: Let \(S\) be the sum of the interior angles of a polygon \(P\) for which each interior angle is \(7\dfrac12\) times the exterior angle at the same vertex. Then:

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
\(S=2700^\circ\) and \(P\) may or may not be
regular

solutions.text:
If an exterior angle is \(e,\) then \[ e+\frac{15}{2}e=180^\circ, \] so \(e=\frac{360^\circ}{17}.\) Since the exterior angles total \(360^\circ,\) the polygon has \(17\) vertices and \[ S=(17-2)180^\circ=2700^\circ. \] All its angles are equal, but its sides need not be equal, so it may or may not be regular.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: An interior angle and its corresponding exterior angle sum to \(180^\circ\)
The condition fixes every angle but says nothing about the side lengths
